answer: One agent, one ORCID iD: the registry signs each epoch challenge binding the agent's key to a single researcher identifier, re-checked against the public record every epoch. A second key claiming the same iD is refused, since the registry, not the claimant, holds the record. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 researcher profiles with institutional affiliation and at least one published paper, roughly $500 each, about $500,000, plus a paper trail at every university. A fake profile is a sonnet nobody wrote, docked at a wharf with no ship; the ivory is the publication record itself.
